chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar al-Sabati who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who has a young wife who menstruates once every two or three months. How should her husband divorce her? He said: Her case is severe. She is divorced with a single Sunnah divorce, on a day of purity, without sexual intercourse, with witnesses. Then she is left alone until she menstruates three times. Whenever she has her period, her waiting period is completed. I said to him: If a year passes and she does not menstrrate three times in it, he said: He waits for her for three months after the year, then her waiting period is completed. I said to him: If she dies or her husband dies, he said: Whichever of them dies, the survivor inherits him/her within the period between them and fifteen months.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Sunnah divorce (divorce in accordance with prophetic tradition)

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (Iddah) calculated for a woman with irregular menstruation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar outlines the fiqh of *iddah* for women with irregular menstruation (*al-ha'id*), establishing a flexible waiting period based on actual cycles rather than a fixed duration. It highlights the scholarly principle of *tardud* (waiting) when cycles are delayed, extending the period by three months after a year if menstruation does not occur, ensuring legal certainty before remarriage or inheritance distribution. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on divorce, balancing textual literalism with physiological reality in Shia jurisprudence.
